questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country had to be culturally interesting to me including the opportunities for further exploration and food culture specifically.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a good introprogram both by the university and the independent student organisation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not exactly easy. I found my housing by chance in a Facebook group. I initially wanted to find housing through the university, but I do not recommend counting on that process.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transport is very often late (unless you take the metro, which is not close to the campus) so try your best to find something in walking distance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I accidentally booked a dorm room in a kind of convent/monastery through the university. Do NOT do that. There is a curfew that essentially means you will miss out on a lot.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was sufficient information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An orientation presentation and a pamphlet.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I unfortunately wanted a class that was fully booked 45 min. after the registration opened. I tried everything to get registered in the class, but the professors have no control and the administration does not budge. So if you didn't get one of your courses, you either have to give up or hope that someone drops the class.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready when registration opens and be 100% sure of your password as the website went down, so it's impossible to recover your password in the middle of the whole process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Especially the master courses were of low academic quality which was not expected at all.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: My bachelor courses were harder than my master courses and that was my general impression from others as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot like the teaching style in Danish high schools.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative politics, The integration of Europe, EU law (terrible course), Financial Statement Analysis and Introduction to Business law. The last two courses I took outside of my study program to get access to another master program.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in extending your knowledge of law, I can definitely recommend the Introduction to Business law course.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Restaurants and grocery shopping were definitely more expensive than I had expected unless you are buying Italian products. Some products were even more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The organisation ESN hosts a lot of fun social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Padel is fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went on some amazing trips in Italy. I would recommend seeing the Dolomites, Sicily and Bari/Matera! I wanted to go to Florence as well but didn't have the time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay. Italians are surprisingly bad at English, so it was hard to fully connect with the culture but that was expected.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are not that open to new people but luckily other exchange students are.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language. Italians are not that good at English and I find it to be a very important factor in bonding with the culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and going out vibe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for the bad public transport, it's part of the experience, you will get tired of pasta and pizza, travel!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't go there for the academics.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling and meeting amazing people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Social expectations.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
